key_insight: A guided diffusion model can reconstruct phase-limited bubbly-flow velocity fields from partial 2D information while preserving realistic turbulence statistics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical generative prior for recovering otherwise unmeasurable multiphase flow data from sparse experiments or incomplete simulations.
method: Train on 2D slices extracted from fully resolved 3D DNS of buoyancy-driven bubbly pseudo-turbulence.
Generate velocity fields both unconditionally and with conditioning on the surrounding liquid-phase flow.
Use simple patching of adjacent 2D slices to extend reconstruction toward 3D bubble-interior fields.
evidence_signal: The reconstructed bubble-phase velocities reproduce key statistical features of the flow and the sliced-patch approach yields a reasonable 3D interior reconstruction.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the availability of representative DNS training data, and patching slices could limit continuity and fidelity in fully 3D structures.
paper_title: Gappy Reconstruction of Bubbly Flows by Guided Diffusion Models
